name: MonarchLoadingState
title: LoadingState
wrapsNative: Text placeholders with redacted(reason: .placeholder), or ProgressView with .progressViewStyle(.circular)
summary: A placeholder for content that is loading: skeleton rows, cards or paragraphs, or a labelled spinner, announced once.
whenToUse: In place of a list, a grid or a detail page during its first load, when the real layout cannot be drawn yet.
whenNotToUse: When the real views can be drawn with sample data, apply redacted(reason: .placeholder) to them instead (see skeleton). For the next page of a list, use MonarchLoadMore. For a load that failed, use MonarchErrorState.
api: init(_ label: String, variant: MonarchLoadingStateVariant = .list, rows: Int = 4)
enum MonarchLoadingStateVariant { case list, rows, cards, detail, spinner }

options.name: label
options.description: What is loading, such as "Loading tickets". Read and announced; shown by the spinner variant.

options.name: variant
options.description: list (avatar and two lines), rows (a line and a short value), cards (a grid of blocks), detail (a title and paragraphs) or spinner.

options.name: rows
options.description: The rows or cards drawn by list, rows and cards. Negative counts draw none.

appearance: Placeholder lines are the system redaction bars drawn with the subtle text colour; avatars and cards are filled with the muted background colour and the container corner radius. The spinner is the system circular ProgressView with the label in muted body text. Nothing moves.
platformNotes: The web skeleton shimmers; the system placeholder on iOS is still, so nothing needs stopping under Reduce Motion. The web marks the region aria-busy; iOS has no busy state, so the label is announced once instead. Android shares the name and the variants.
accessibility: The view is one element read as the label; the placeholders are hidden from VoiceOver.
The label is announced once when the view appears.
The spinner variant also shows the label.
Placeholder lines are text, so their height follows Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: Placeholder lines are one line each and are cut at the edge at the largest text sizes.
Card columns are at least 160 points wide, so a phone in portrait shows two columns.
Showing the view again announces the label again; keep it on screen for the whole load.
